cases.title: Half marathon under 1:30, never run, one day a week (mine)

input.goal: Finish a half marathon in under 1 hour 30 minutes
input.baseline: I have never run. I can't jog for more than a minute.

coachNote.message: With no running experience and a one-minute jogging limit, one day a week cannot prepare you safely for a sub-1:30 half marathon. A first honest plan needs at least 3 days a week, and that target remains too ambitious to promise from this baseline.

cases.title: First half marathon, one day a week (mine)

input.baseline: I run 3 km once a week at an easy pace.

asked.question: Do you have a finish time in mind?

coachNote.message: A first half marathon needs at least 3 runs a week, so both plans use 3–4. Your current once-weekly 3 km is a starting point, so allow time to build gradually.

options.rationale: A gradual 20-week progression toward finishing your first half marathon, with three easy running days each week to start. The goal is to finish; no time target was chosen.
assumptions: Runs are kept easy and guided by conversational effort because no numeric easy pace was provided.
The plan progresses toward longer continuous runs, with recovery and cutback periods as needed.
Adjust or pause sessions if you cannot complete them comfortably; this plan cannot guarantee race completion.
